edits.speaker: Customer 1
edits.known: I'd like large, please. With oat milk if you have it.
edits.from: Željela bih veliku, molim. S zobenim mlijekom ako imate.
edits.to: Željela bih veliku, molim. Sa zobenim mlijekom, ako imate.
edits.why: sa before z — sibling SC08-S015 "sa sirom", SC06-S011 "sa suprugom"

edits.speaker: Guest
edits.known: Good afternoon. I have a booking under the name Jones.
edits.from: Dobro podne. Imam rezervaciju… na ime Jones.
edits.to: Dobar dan. Imam rezervaciju… na ime Jones.
edits.why: "Dobro podne" is not standard Croatian; siblings SC03-S001/S002 render "Good afternoon" as "Dobar dan"

edits.speaker: Customer 1
edits.known: Excuse me - do you have anything gluten-free? Or for vegetarians?
edits.from: Izvinite —… imate li nešto… bez glutena? Ili za… vegetarijance?
edits.to: Oprostite,… imate li nešto… bez glutena? Ili za… vegetarijance?
edits.why: "Izvinite" is Serbian; siblings SC02-S001/SC10-S001 render "Excuse me" as "Oprostite"

edits.speaker: Tourist
edits.known: Excuse me, do you know how to get to the nearest supermarket?
edits.from: Izvinite, znate li… kako doći do najbližeg… supermarketa?
edits.to: Oprostite, znate li… kako doći do najbližeg… supermarketa?
edits.why: same Serbianism, same sibling evidence

edits.speaker: Customer 2
edits.known: A bottle of the house red would be lovely.
edits.from: Jedna boca kućnog… crvenog bila bi divna.
edits.to: Jedna boca kućnog… crnog bila bi divna.
edits.why: red wine is crno vino in Croatian — siblings SC08-S009 "crnog vina", SC08-S007 "kućno crno"

edits.speaker: Local
edits.known: You'll see the supermarket on your left, just opposite the bus stop.
edits.from: Vidjet ćete supermarket… s lijeve strane, točno… nasuprot autobusnog… stajališta.
edits.to: Vidjet ćete supermarket… s lijeve strane, točno… nasuprot autobusnom… stajalištu.
edits.why: nasuprot governs the dative, not the genitive

edits.speaker: Narrator
edits.known: 19. 20. 21. Wednesday. Thursday.
edits.from: 19. 20. 21. Srijeda. Četvrtak.
edits.to: Devetnaest. Dvadeset. Dvadeset i jedan. Srijeda. Četvrtak.
edits.why: digit + full stop is the Croatian ordinal — TTS reads "19." as devetnaesti; siblings are spelled out

edits.speaker: Narrator
edits.known: 100. 200. 1000. Sunday. 12 o'clock.
edits.from: 100. 200. 1000. Nedjelja. 12 sati.
edits.to: Sto. Dvjesto. Tisuća. Nedjelja. Dvanaest sati.
edits.why: same ordinal trap; nominative citation form matches sibling SC13-S011

edits.speaker: Customer 3
edits.known: Good morning. Two Americanos and a cup of tea, please.
edits.from: Dobro jutro. Dva americána… i jednu šalicu čaja,… molim.
edits.to: Dobro jutro. Dva americana… i jednu šalicu čaja,… molim.
edits.why: á is not a Croatian letter — the acute is a Spanish import and mis-cues TTS

edits.speaker: Customer 3
edits.known: Could I see the wine list? I want a glass of wine.
edits.from: Mogu li vidjeti kartu vina? Želim čašu vina.
edits.to: Mogu li vidjeti vinsku kartu? Želim čašu vina.
edits.why: this pod renders "wine list" as vinska karta at SC09-S012 — ZUT

edits.speaker: Sarah
edits.known: Good afternoon. I'd like a coffee, please. With milk but with no sugar. To take away.
edits.from: Dobar dan. Željela bih kavu, molim. S mlijekom ali bez šećera. Za van.
edits.to: Dobar dan. Željela bih kavu, molim. S mlijekom, ali bez šećera. Za van.
edits.why: Croatian orthography requires a comma before ali

edits.speaker: Sarah
edits.known: Hello! I'm sorry but I can't talk at the moment. I need to go home now. Can we talk tomorrow?
edits.from: Bok! Žao mi je ali ne mogu sada razgovarati. Moram sada ići kući. Možemo li razgovarati sutra?
edits.to: Bok! Žao mi je, ali ne mogu sada razgovarati. Moram sada ići kući. Možemo li razgovarati sutra?
edits.why: same rule — comma before ali is obligatory

edits.speaker: Learner
edits.known: I prefer to try to speak your language, I think it's polite.
edits.from: Radije bih pokušala govoriti vaš jezik, mislim da je to pristojno.
edits.to: Radije bih pokušao govoriti vaš jezik, mislim da je to pristojno.
edits.why: Learner is masculine in the recorded scene 22 (siguran / izrazio / sretan)

edits.speaker: Learner
edits.known: You spoke a little too quickly, so I'm not sure if I understood.
edits.from: Govorili ste malo prebrzo, pa nisam sigurna jesam li razumjela.
edits.to: Govorili ste malo prebrzo, pa nisam siguran jesam li razumio.
edits.why: same speaker as recorded SC22-S005 "Nisam siguran"

edits.speaker: Learner
edits.known: That makes me happy.
edits.from: To me čini sretnom.
edits.to: To me čini sretnim.
edits.why: masculine instrumental, matching recorded SC22-S011 "sretan"

edits.speaker: Learner
edits.known: I'd like two scoops of ice-cream, please.
edits.from: Željela bih dvije kuglice sladoleda, molim.
edits.to: Želio bih dvije kuglice sladoleda, molim.
edits.why: Learner gender — masculine conditional

edits.speaker: Learner
edits.known: Yes, I said it's over there.
edits.from: Da, rekla sam da je tamo.
edits.to: Da, rekao sam da je tamo.
edits.why: Learner gender

edits.speaker: Learner
edits.known: Is there a cash machine near here?
edits.from: Ima li bankomat blizu ovdje?
edits.to: Ima li tu negdje bankomat?
edits.why: "blizu ovdje" is not Croatian word order; recorded sibling SC13-S008 gives the natural form

edits.speaker: Narrator
edits.to: Sto tisuća. Šezdeset. Sedamdeset. Jedan sat. Jedanaest sati.
edits.why: digit + full stop is the Croatian ordinal — TTS reads "60." as šezdeseti

edits.speaker: Narrator
edits.known: A million. 80. 90. 2 o'clock. 10 o'clock.
edits.from: Milijun. 80. 90. 2 sata. 10 sati.
edits.to: Milijun. Osamdeset. Devedeset. Dva sata. Deset sati.
edits.why: same; siblings spell numbers out in words

edits.speaker: Narrator
edits.known: 3 o'clock. 9 o'clock. January. February.
edits.from: 3 sata. 9 sati. Siječanj. Veljača.
edits.to: Tri sata. Devet sati. Siječanj. Veljača.
edits.why: same

edits.speaker: Narrator
edits.known: 4 o'clock. 8 o'clock. March. April.
edits.from: 4 sata. 8 sati. Ožujak. Travanj.
edits.to: Četiri sata. Osam sati. Ožujak. Travanj.
edits.why: same

edits.speaker: Narrator
edits.known: 5 o'clock. 7 o'clock. May. June.
edits.from: 5 sati. 7 sati. Svibanj. Lipanj.
edits.to: Pet sati. Sedam sati. Svibanj. Lipanj.
edits.why: same

edits.speaker: Narrator
edits.known: 6 o'clock. July. August. September.
edits.from: 6 sati. Srpanj. Kolovoz. Rujan.
edits.to: Šest sati. Srpanj. Kolovoz. Rujan.
edits.why: same
